title: second-shift consumer-repo configuration (static context)
description: The single per-repo onboarding file (.claude/second-shift.config.json). Everything repo-specific that the generic plugins need: tracker, the command truth table, reviewer registry deltas, paths, the design axis and the scheduler's caps. Domain knowledge does NOT belong here — it lives in repo-local skills and extension files (see docs/extension-points.md).

$schema.description: Optional editor-validation pointer; onboard writes the schema URL at the pinned marketplace ref.

configVersion.description: Schema version of this config file; bumped only on breaking schema changes. The upgrade from 2 is docs/migrations/v2-to-v3.md.

writes.description: Whether the build and review sessions may write to the tracker. The annotated default is github's; the runtime default is false for any other tracker. A false value starts /dev-pipeline:run's sessions without Atlassian write tools; under github the scheduler still swaps the claim labels, posts the claim marker and posts the closing comment. The ticket read stays active regardless.

branchPrefix.description: Branch-name namespace prepended to the ticket key: the work branch is "<branchPrefix><ticketKey>" (a jira key lowercased). Read by tools/branch-prefix.sh, which /dev-pipeline:run calls; it refuses to guess when the key is absent. github example: "claude/acme-" (→ claude/acme-42). JIRA example: a per-user identifier plus a slash, e.g. "jdoe/" (→ jdoe/gh-540).

bot.description: Dedicated bot identity for the pipeline's GitHub writes: PR comments and markers, the git committer, and — under tracker.type github only — the claim. Legal under either tracker.type, because source control is GitHub for every adapter, so a JIRA-tracked repo writes to GitHub too and needs the identity just as much. The key sits under `tracker` for historical reasons; its scope is the code host.

wrapperPath.description: Explicit path to the gh-as-bot wrapper script. When set, install-gh-bot.sh writes it here and claim-issue.sh's GH_BOT default resolves to it, instead of the $HOME/.config/<repo-basename>/gh-as-bot.sh derivation (which was derived wrong once — a canary catch). Supports $HOME/~ expansion.

app.description: GitHub App identity for the bot (previously hardcoded in install-gh-bot.sh with no config home). Onboarding a different repo's bot app sets these instead of editing script constants.

appName.description: GitHub App slug, e.g. "acme-dev-pipeline" (used in settings-page URLs and messages).

privateKeyFilename.description: Private-key filename installed under the bot config dir, e.g. "acme-dev-pipeline.private-key.pem".

installationId.description: Optional: pin the installation ID to skip API discovery.

keyPattern.description: Regex for ticket keys as used in branch names and record filenames (e.g. "[A-Z]+-[0-9]+" for JIRA, "[0-9]+" for GitHub issue numbers). /dev-pipeline:run refuses a key that does not match (branch-prefix.sh reads the same pattern). Absent = accept any non-empty key.

labels.description: github only: the queue/claim/blocker label vocabulary by ROLE. Read by /dev-pipeline:run (the queue check, the blocker skip and the claim swap) and claim-issue.sh. Absent → the shipped defaults.

queue.description: The label the pipeline picks work from and drops at claim. A crashed claim swap can leave it behind, so the unclaim workflow /second-shift:onboard emits also releases it when the item CLOSES. Default "ready-for-dev".

claimed.description: The label added atomically at claim. It stays on while the work is in flight, including through review, and is released when the tracker item CLOSES, by the unclaim workflow /second-shift:onboard emits. Default "in-progress".

blockers.description: Labels that block auto-pickup (an issue carrying any is skipped). Default ["epic","needs-intake-review","needs-spec-work","needs-plan-review"].

commands.description: Command truth table keyed by an id. /dev-pipeline:run uses the sole key, else the key equal to the main checkout's directory name (a linked worktree resolves to its main checkout); nothing cross-checks the ids. null = check not available in this repo.

allowUnverified.description: Zero-check safety valve. When no check is configured (lint/typecheck/test/format all null, no extraLanes) and the ticket record declares no ## Checks, /dev-pipeline:run treats the round as red — unless this is true, which declares the opt-out deliberate. Inert when any check is configured.

lanes.description: SETUP-only steps (e.g. dependency install, workspace-package builds) run by /dev-pipeline:run in order, fail-fast, BEFORE the checks, after every build. Each entry's cwd is a path under the ticket worktree. Do not put a check here; additive checks are extraLanes.

extraLanes.description: Additive checks, run by /dev-pipeline:run after lint/typecheck/test/format on every build. Every one blocks: a red one spends one attempt on the checks-red counter (run.checksRedMax), and its log goes to the next build session.

name.description: kebab-case, unique; names the lane in the check log.

when.description: Changed-file globs: the lane runs when any file changed on the branch matches one. Empty/absent = always run.

failureClass.description: A closed failure-taxonomy value, kept as a label for the lane. It no longer changes behavior: every configured lane blocks.

reviewers.description: Deltas against the plugin-shipped review-lead registry.

add.description: Repo-local reviewer agents (in this repo's .claude/agents/) to register with review-lead.

dimensions.description: Review dimensions this agent covers (dedup/routing hint for review-lead).

remove.description: Plugin-shipped reviewers to disable in this repo (e.g. db-reviewer in an FE repo).

default.description: Plugin-shipped reviewers this repo dispatches UNCONDITIONALLY on the pipeline path, on top of the default panel (/dev-pipeline:review's fan-out defaults to scope-completeness-reviewer; security-reviewer, a11y-reviewer and unit-test-mutation-reviewer are opt-in). Purely ADDITIVE — dropping a shipped reviewer stays reviewers.remove's job. Names are the plugin-shipped bare names; config-lint.sh types the array and check-reviewer-references.sh validates the names against the review-lead registry.

modelOverrides.description: Per-agent model-tier override, keyed by any agent the .mjs dispatch tables model — the review-lead panel reviewers, the intake fan-out agents, and the structured-emitter transcription sink. check-model-tiers validates .mjs tables against frontmatter + these overrides. Values must be tiers this consumer's subscription can actually dispatch — an inaccessible tier surfaces as a dead reviewer. `fable` is override-only: never a shipped default, and a check-model-tiers error if it appears in a shipped dispatch table.

additionalProperties.description: A dispatch model (haiku, sonnet, opus, fable) OR a tier name from the effective reviewers.tierMap. That union is a cross-field constraint JSON Schema cannot express — it depends on a sibling property — so this half asserts only "string" and config-lint.sh carries the real check, including typo detection. Do not re-add an enum here: it would reject every legal tier name.

tierMap.description: Retarget an abstract tier to a different dispatch model. MERGES per tier over the plugin-shipped alphabet in review-toolkit's model-tiering.md, so a config naming one tier leaves the rest at their defaults. Shipped dispatch tables name tiers rather than vendor tokens, so a consumer whose subscription lacks a model class retargets it here instead of forking the plugin.

webComponentGlobs.description: The web-component surface: the globs whose presence in the diff route the a11y reviewer and the design-fidelity reviewer (read by review-lead when it selects the panel). Set this when the FE is not React-under-apps/web — e.g. ["src/app/**/*.{html,ts}"] (Angular), ["src/**/*.vue"] (Vue), ["app/**/*.tsx"] (React Router v7).

plansDir.description: Directory (worktree-relative) holding the committed intake record, <plansDir>/<repo>-<key>-decisions.md, which /dev-pipeline:run commits as the branch's first commit.

pipelineStateDir.description: Where /dev-pipeline:run keeps run logs and reads the pre-flight receipt (<pipelineStateDir>/<key>-ledger.md), relative to the main checkout.

design.description: Optional design-fidelity axis. Selects the design-toolkit adapter family. Key absent = design fidelity off.

provider.description: figma → figma-faithful skills + Figma-MCP prerequisite; claude-design → design-faithful skills + DesignSync prerequisite.

liveRender.description: The repo's render and smoke commands. After every build, /dev-pipeline:run runs the route smoke for each `## Design frames` row of the ticket record: command renders the row (a missing image, or two states rendering identically, is red), then smokeCommand checks the row's must-show value. A red smoke spends one attempt on the checks-red counter (run.checksRedMax), and its log goes to the next build session. The build and review sessions may run command too. See docs/live-render.md.

command.description: Repo-owned render script with {route} and {out} placeholders, plus an optional {state}, e.g. "yarn render:verify --route {route} --state {state} --out {out}". The harness owns boot/auth/screenshot and must emit a PNG at {out}, exiting nonzero with a clear message on failure. Placeholders must appear UNQUOTED — each substituted value is shell-quoted. See docs/live-render.md.

smokeCommand.description: Repo-owned smoke command with {route} and {mustShow} placeholders, run by /dev-pipeline:run after every build for each `## Design frames` row, after command renders it: it must exit non-zero unless the route renders and shows that row's must-show value (a data-test id or a copy string). A record that declares design frames while this or command is absent stops the run as env-smoke-unconfigured.

readyProbe.description: Optional URL curl-checked (three tries) before the route smoke renders (e.g. a sibling BE health endpoint). Not ready stops the run as env-not-ready instead of reporting a failed render.

run.description: Per-ticket caps for /dev-pipeline:run. Every key optional; env overrides config overrides the default.

checksRedMax.description: Red check or smoke attempts before checks-red-spent, on their own counter (default 3).

costCeilingUsd.description: Sum of the sessions' total_cost_usd before cost-spent (default 100).
